newsitem.title: USA: SUNGLASS HUT SAYS INVENTORY/DEBT DECLINE.
newsitem.headline: SUNGLASS HUT SAYS INVENTORY/DEBT DECLINE.

text.p: Sunglass Hut International said Thursday it's plans for reducing inventory levels and debt are running on schedule, helped in part by the summer movie hit, "Men In Black".
The sunglasses retailer said it was "pleased with the progress made in its inventory management efforts as well as the resulting improvement in corporate liquidity."
Sunglass Hut said inventory levels were cut to $115 million from $145 million since the start of the year.

The company added that its revolving debt borrowings, which stood at $50 million at the start of the year, were paid back in full by the end of the second quarter, helped in large part by increased working capital efficiencies and the seasonally strong second quarter cash flow.
A portion of the July sales success was attributed to the the success of "Men in Black", which, the company said "spurred" the sales of Bausch & Lomb's Ray Ban Predator line of sunglasses.

However, the company clouded the report, reminding investors its ongoing plan to reduce and refresh inventory levels was expected to cut gross profit margins in the second quarter and to a lesser extent for the balance of the year.
